title: 18th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened at 9:02 with the President's nomination of a Maldives Monetary Authority governor being sent to the Finance Committee. Members then wrapped up debate on two government bills: an amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act (bail rules, court-ordered interception of private communications, electronic evidence, cybercrime) and an amendment to the law on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters. Both bills were accepted for study and sent to the Judiciary Committee with no votes against, and the House also approved the Government Oversight Committee's report on the President's ministries.

items.title: Opening prayer and start of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 53 present, 4 on leave, 10 on official travel (as announced by the chair)

items.title: President's nomination of a Maldives Monetary Authority governor (Ahmed Munawar)
Bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act (Law 12/2016), sponsored by the member for Manadhoo
items.outcome: debated to the end; accepted 72-0, sent to Judiciary Committee

items.title: Bill to amend the Act on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters (Law 2/2015), sponsored by the member for Holhudhoo
items.outcome: debated; accepted 71-0, sent to Judiciary Committee

items.title: Government Oversight Committee report on the ministries and work areas set up by the President on 17 Nov 2023
Votes (three)
items.outcome: all three passed with no votes against

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Praised the amendments and the President's justice agenda, and criticised the opposition for low participation in debate.
Said court backlogs and slow case handling by the Prosecutor General leave people jailed too long, and that courthouse repairs should be fixed.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: As bill sponsor, said interception of private communications must only happen under a court order, with officers accountable for misuse.
Asked the committee to set a fixed time limit for courts to decide bail requests, saying the bill lacks one.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: On the Criminal Procedure bill, said interception targets serious crimes such as terrorism and trafficking, under court order, and police must stay professional.
On his mutual legal assistance bill, said cross-border cybercrime needs clear steps for sharing information, and asked for quick committee study and passage.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: As committee rapporteur, presented the Government Oversight Committee report on the ministries and work areas created in Nov 2023.
Said the report was passed unanimously by members present and the committee is answering citizens' letters.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Backed the bill and urged faster trials, saying long pre-trial detention of people later cleared is unjust.
Argued crime prevention, including values taught in schools, matters alongside enforcement.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Defended the bill as an important government reform on cybercrime and bail.
Said the opposition should have joined the debate, and proposed sending the bill to committee.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Welcomed the bail provisions at trial and appeal stage, citing people jailed then acquitted.
Warned the amendments only help if investigators and judges apply them in good faith.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Called the bill technical and urged all members to debate it with expert input.
Warned that innocent people could be caught up in cybercrime cases, and that bail deposits and loopholes need care.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Supported the bill as modernising law for a digital age, including accepting electronic evidence such as email and phones.
Acknowledged privacy concerns but said the bill contains protections.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Focused on the cybercrime parts, citing attacks on state-owned company networks in January.
Said the committee should look at how to identify who owns a phone or IT device used in a crime.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shifaz
positions: Said the bill touches cybercrime and bail, and that banking systems also need strengthening.
Asked that bail relief for people held without trial be applied lawfully, including around elections.

decisions: President's nomination of a Maldives Monetary Authority governor referred to the Finance Committee.
Criminal Procedure Act amendment bill accepted by the House (72 yes) and sent to the Judiciary Committee.
Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters amendment bill accepted (71 yes) and sent to the Judiciary Committee.
Government Oversight Committee report on the President's ministries and work areas approved (70 yes).
Next sitting set for 24 July 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept Criminal Procedure Act (12/2016) amendment bill
Accept Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters Act (2/2015) amendment bill
Approve ministries and work areas established 17 Nov 2023 (Government Oversight Committee report)
